name: Explanatory how come

1.definition: Asks for an explanation of an actual or apparently actual state of affairs.

projection.target: Ordinary why questions allow Why is the gate open? How come normally retains subject-before-auxiliary order in the corresponding main-clause question.
projection.evidence: See the cited discussion and the constructed illustration.

curious.title: How come
curious.summary: How come asks for an explanation of something that seems to be the case.
curious.body: How come the gate is open? asks why the gate is open. It treats the open gate as a fact that needs explaining. The pattern differs from an ordinary why question. Why is the gate open? puts the verb before the subject. How come keeps the subject first: how come the gate is open.
curious.try: Ask the same question with Why and with How come. Which word order does each one use?

teacher.summary: Shows learners how come as a way to ask for an explanation, with different word order from why.
teacher.explain: How come plus a subject and finite predicate asks for an explanation of an actual or apparently actual state of affairs: How come the gate is open? An ordinary why question allows Why is the gate open?, with the verb before the subject. How come normally keeps subject-before-auxiliary order in the corresponding main-clause question. This dictionary relates it to open interrogative clauses and marks the analysis as provisional.
teacher.terms: Open interrogative is this dictionary’s term for questions with a question word, traditionally wh-questions.

contrasts.text: How come the gate is open?

watch_for: A learner might read How come as asking in what way something happened.
A learner might put the verb first after how come, as after why.
teacher.activity: Give students a set of observed situations (a light on, a late bus). They ask each with Why and with How come, and mark where the subject sits.

child.hook: What is another way to ask why?
child.explain: How come can ask why. How come the gate is open? means the same as asking why it is open. How come starts the question, then the gate comes next.
child.play: Ask a friend about something odd you see with How come. Then ask with Why and notice which words move.

cite: Reynolds, Brett, ed. 2026. "Explanatory how come." English Constructionary. https://brettreynolds.ca/constructionary/linguist/how-come-explanation-001/ (snapshot 2026-11-19, ef810bb).
